answer.rationale: The 18% mandate cannot be met by the incumbent, who already refused to reopen price this cycle (closing off negotiate_terms as a standalone path), and the contract lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew, so deferring risks an involuntary gap in primary supply while the line runs at 94% with no buffer. memory_c2 is the only precedent directly supporting switch_primary_vendor and claims quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, but it's a single-instance, year-old record that says nothing about performance under tight capacity/no-buffer conditions, so I want its original source verified before treating it as reliable grounds for a full cutover. Given the delivery-risk stakes, I'm scoping this as a small guarded test of the low-cost vendor on a limited volume/SKU slice rather than a broad rollout, so we can validate quality and delivery reliability before committing the whole line to them, while a fallback (short-term extension or second-source contingency) is preserved for the next review cycle.
